prize_parts.citation: for the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules recruit ubiquitin ligases to destroy chosen proteins, from bifunctional PROTACs to cereblon-based molecular glues

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single prize part on targeted protein degradation for Crews, Deshaies and Handa. The principle is simple to state and it is a game-changer by the standard I apply: a small molecule brings a ubiquitin ligase to a protein and the cell destroys it. This reaches targets with no active site to occupy, and it also explains how thalidomide and its analogues act through cereblon. The design logic (ternary-complex formation, ligand optimisation, ligase recruitment) has been reproduced in many independent laboratories and extended to new ligases and targets. Round 1 showed that this is the only configuration that four of eight members already carry, and that the open questions among them are about citation scope, the third name and clinical record, not about the science. On the chair's question of one achievement or two, I think one is defensible if the citation names the shared principle, hijacking the ubiquitin-proteasome system by induced proximity, and does not claim that Handa's work is PROTAC chemistry. Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the PROTAC concept; Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, which is what makes the glue branch a mechanism rather than an observation. I keep Handa over Ciulli because the glue branch is the most clinically validated part of the field today.
statement.case_against: The strongest objections stand. No PROTAC drug is approved as far as I know (an unverified claim that the experts should check), so the field's clinical vindication rests on molecular glues of the thalidomide class and on trials. Credit is spread over eight names and the three-person cap excludes Ciulli (VHL ligands and the structural basis of ternary complexes), Gray, Sakamoto, Ito and Kim, which will be contested. Somfai's point is fair that the cereblon discovery is a target-identification result rather than new synthetic chemistry, and a single citation risks being either vague or unfair to one of the two strands. The field is also still moving quickly, so a later prize might be better informed.

responses.point: Chabes would credit only Crews and Deshaies for degradation, pair it with base editing for Liu alone, and accept Handa as a third name only if the committee prefers a single achievement.
responses.response: I agree that the PROTAC concept is carried cleanly by Crews and Deshaies, and I accept that the two-part reading is coherent as chemical biology. I still cannot support it, for two reasons. First, a Crews and Deshaies citation leaves out the cereblon mechanism, which is the most clinically validated half of degradation and the part that explains a drug that harmed and then helped patients. Second, sole credit to Liu does not survive the record: Komor and Gaudelli carried out the decisive editor experiments, Kondo and Nishida reported an independent deaminase editor, and the 2020 prize makes base editing look like a refinement of an already rewarded platform. If the committee wants one achievement, which you say you could accept, then your own condition is met by my configuration with Handa as the third name. I changed nothing here, but your question on mechanism has sharpened my citation wording.

responses.point: Brzezinski prefers nitrogenase for Rees, Einsle and Seefeldt as a mature, attributable structure-to-mechanism story, and concedes that the catalytic cycle is only partly resolved.
responses.response: I share your respect for this problem; it is the kind of mechanism-under-biology question I enjoy, and the FeMo-cofactor and carbide structures are firmly established. My reservation is the one you name: the E4 state, the substrate-binding site and the order of proton and electron delivery are not settled, so a citation on mechanism would honour something unfinished, and one on structure alone would struggle to justify why Seefeldt rather than Dean or Ribbe. I would only support B032 if the experts confirm that a citation can rest on cofactor structure and function. I have moved it into my alternatives, replacing B037, because I find it more mature than genetic code expansion and because your argument on attribution is the more concrete.

responses.point: Aili proposes the same trio for B044 but ties the citation to the cereblon glue mechanism of thalidomide-class drugs and weighs clinical vindication against the established mechanism.
responses.response: We agree on the trio and on the maturity question: mechanism and independent reproduction across laboratories seem to me sufficient even without an approved PROTAC. I prefer a citation that states the induced-proximity principle with PROTACs and glues as its two expressions, rather than leading with cereblon, because a cereblon-led wording makes Crews and Deshaies look like an afterthought. I do accept your point that the glue mechanism should be named explicitly, and I have added cereblon to my citation.

responses.point: Sparr prefers biomolecular phase separation for Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen as a physical-chemical principle of cell organisation.
responses.response: I still consider the concept important and the attribution neat. My question remains quantitative: which condensates at endogenous concentrations in living cells are demonstrated equilibrium phases, and which predictions of the framework were tested there rather than in vitro? Until the committee sees that, I would not rank B039 above a mechanism that has already changed what chemists can do.

uncertainties: Whether the expert reports and the committee accept one citation covering both PROTACs and cereblon-based glues, or whether the two strands are better treated as separate achievements.

Whether Handa or Ciulli should hold the third place; I choose Handa on clinical validation and the thalidomide mechanism, but Ciulli's structural work on ternary complexes is the stronger contribution to rational design.
Whether the lack of an approved PROTAC drug should count against the prize this year, and whether it is true at all.
Whether degradation can reach five votes when four members support it and the other four prefer four different single ballots.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict requiring recusal. My postdoc link to Warshel (empirical valence bond) is unrelated to any shortlisted credited name. As a computational chemist I have a field affinity with B020 (Car and Parrinello) and a scientific interest in B032 as an enzymologist, and I weigh both only as alternatives. I have no personal or institutional tie to Crews, Deshaies, Handa or any other credited name.
